claims.text: The feedstock is gas-atomized AlCrFeNiSi powder with a metastable as-atomized microstructure and typical composition distribution.
AlCrFeNiSi powder can be processed into miniature components by laser powder bed fusion.
Controlled in-situ substrate preheating at 400–600 °C is the proposed intervention.
The proposed intervention is applicable to AlCrFeNiSi miniature components smaller than 1 cm.
The applicable LPBF regime uses optimized scan speeds, low energy densities, and an inert atmosphere.
Substrate preheating decreases the thermal gradient during layer deposition.
Decreasing the thermal gradient reduces rapid cooling rates.
Reduced thermal gradients and cooling rates lower residual thermal stresses in LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
The moderated thermal environment produces a more uniform phase distribution and less microstructural heterogeneity.
Preheating may promote beneficial local chemical short-range ordering in AlCrFeNiSi.
Chemical short-range order can influence dislocation mobility.
Reduced lattice distortion and enhanced short-range-order effects improve the ductility and yield strength of LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Preheated specimens will have lower residual stresses than specimens built at ambient substrate temperature.
Preheated specimens will have a more homogeneous microstructure than specimens built at ambient substrate temperature.
Preheated specimens will exhibit higher yield strength than specimens built at ambient substrate temperature.
Preheated specimens will exhibit higher ductility than specimens built at ambient substrate temperature.
Substrate preheating will simplify thermal management during LPBF processing.
Ambient-temperature LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi typically produces steep thermal gradients, high residual stresses, and degraded mechanical performance.
The benefits may vary with part geometry, build size, and alloy thermal properties.
Holding laser power, scan speed, layer thickness, and atmosphere constant permits a controlled comparison of ambient and preheated substrates.

contradictions.description: The comparator is described as conventional high-thermal-load LPBF, but the controlled experiment holds laser parameters constant and changes only substrate temperature. It is therefore unclear whether the baseline differs in overall thermal load or only in substrate preheating.
